Split the conjunction.

1. For primes \(p,q\), represent \(pq\) by its prime factorization. Additivity of prime-factor multiplicity under multiplication, together with each prime having exactly one prime factor, gives
\[
\Omega(pq)=\Omega(p)+\Omega(q)=1+1=2.
\]
This is precisely `Nat.IsAlmostPrime 2 (p * q)`, including the case \(p=q\).

2. For a surjective ring homomorphism \(f:R\to S\), use the ideal correspondence: every ideal \(I\subseteq S\) is determined by its inverse image,
\[
\operatorname{map} f(\operatorname{comap} f I)=I.
\]
Hence `Ideal.comap f` reflects both equality and strict inclusion. Since the order on `PrimeSpectrum` is induced by the corresponding prime ideals, if \(P<Q\) in \(\operatorname{Spec} S\), monotonicity gives
\(\operatorname{comap} f P\le \operatorname{comap} f Q\); equality would imply \(P=Q\) after applying `Ideal.map f`, contradicting strictness. Thus `PrimeSpectrum.comap f` is strictly monotone.

Surjectivity is essential in the second part: without it, distinct prime ideals of \(S\) can have the same contraction to \(R\).
